headings.text: English for Job Interviews: Questions and Best Answers
"Where do you see yourself in 5 years?"

paragraphs: Ace your next interview. Common questions, strong answer structures, and the phrases that show confidence in English.
Interviews test English more than you think. Clear, structured answers win. Here are the most common questions with answer frameworks.
Use the 4-part formula: name, background, experience, goal. Keep it under 60 seconds.
Show you researched the company. "I admire your focus on simple products, and my skills in web development fit your team."
Give one strength with an example. "I am consistent. For example, I practised coding daily and shipped 3 projects."
Pick a real one with a fix. "I used to avoid speaking English, but now I practise 15 minutes every day."
Show growth. "I want to lead small projects and keep learning new tools."
Sit straight. Smile. Make eye contact. Say "Thank you for the question" before answering — it buys thinking time.
Record mock answers with the SpeakNow app. Listen for filler words like "um", "actually", "you know". Reduce them each week.
Confidence comes from preparation, not talent.
